newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH MULL CHANGE TO TAXES ON SHARE BUY-BACKS.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH MULL CHANGE TO TAXES ON SHARE BUY-BACKS.

text.p: The Dutch Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it was studying a request for a change in the tax treatment of share buy-backs.
A ministry spokeswoman said the request came from Royal Dutch Petroleum officials who visited the ministry earlier this year. "We are studying it," she told Reuters.
Royal Dutch owns 60 percent and Shell Transport and Trading 40 percent of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
Shell said last week the Anglo-Dutch group was in talks with the Dutch authorities about share buy-backs which, it added, were not worthwhile in view of the stringent tax laws.
The company said Royal Dutch would look into a buy-back once the Dutch tax regime changed.
The spokeswoman said the ministry acknowledged that the tax laws posed problems for companies considering buying their own shares.
"We are trying to do (whatever is) possible," she added.
Under Dutch laws, tax is levied on the difference between the buy-back price and the nominal value of the shares, which is generally very low, rather than the original purchase price.
Analysts said a buy-back would allow the group to exploit its 6.9 billion stg cash holding.
They said the oil industry was becoming overcapitalised with insufficient suitable opportunities for companies to invest their growing cash flows.
